subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but launching `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` and writing prompt drafts to disk crosses a local process and sensitive-content boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX And Safety Contract
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the permanent trigger and document the local editor/temp-file rules.

options.title: Decline External Process Handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or plugin-owned editing rather than launching local editors from the TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest TUI ownership/history signal and already supplied the clearest prior review framing the remaining product and security decision.
